prompt: Measure how unsorted an array is. Complete countInversions (pairs where a bigger value sits before a smaller one) and firstOutOfOrderIndex.
explanation: An inversion is any pair of positions i < j where values[i] > values[j], so a nested loop over every such pair counts them directly. The total is accumulated into a long because even a thousand elements can produce hundreds of thousands of inversions. firstOutOfOrderIndex only needs neighbours, so a single pass finds the first place where the array stops being non-decreasing, or -1 when it never does.
hints: For countInversions, the outer loop picks i and the inner loop picks every j after it -- count the pairs where values[i] > values[j].
Accumulate into a long, not an int, and make sure you return a long so large arrays cannot overflow.
firstOutOfOrderIndex needs only one pass comparing values[i] with values[i + 1]; equal neighbours are still in order, so return -1 when the scan finishes.
